Switching Auto Insurance Providers: The Pros And Cons Explained

TB
By Tyler Brooks Viral Concepts & Prototype Lead • via Jalopnik Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Jalopnik Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • Chances are pretty high that, if you're reading this, you've got auto insurance.
  • Chances are also pretty high that you think you're spending a bit more than you should be on it.
  • You're not alone — insurance premiums have been steadily rising for the past couple of years across the whole country.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • TYLER BROOKS Viral Concepts & Prototype Lead

Big Picture: Market reception and formal OEM production announcements will determine which concept innovations make it to consumer streets.

Chances are pretty high that, if you're reading this, you've got auto insurance. Chances are also pretty high that you think you're spending a bit more than you should be on it. You're not alone — insurance premiums have been steadily rising for the past couple of years across the whole country. Higher prices on new cars, more tech, and more expensive repairs all contribute to the problem of rising auto insurance rates.

📌 The Core Development

What's a person to do? Well, switching auto insurance providers is one way to get yourself a lower premium, often for identical or nearly identical coverage. When people switch auto insurance it's often because the new company has discounts the old one just doesn't offer, or is running promotions to win over new customers. Sometimes a review of the kinds of coverage you're paying for, and what you're actually using, can reveal places to find savings too. Of course, great rewards frequently have some challenges baked in.

Switching auto insurance providers can be a quick and easy process, but there are some pros and cons to consider before you make the jump. Let's get into it!

🔍 Background & Sector Context

This is the headliner, and it's pretty obvious: you can save money by switching your auto insurance provider! Really, though, you don't have to switch providers to save money — you could reduce the amount of coverage you have, increase your deductible, or skip some of the add-ons like a lower glass deductible or rental car coverage.

Many companies offer new customers deals and discounts to entice them to move from a competitor. Be sure to get quotes not only for auto, but for bundles that the company offers, as some significantly discount their premiums when a customer also purchases renters or homeowners insurance. Some auto insurance companies may also offer lower premiums with programs not offered at your current insurer, like discounts for safe driving when you allow them to monitor your habits with an app or device that attaches to your car.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

Yep, there are a few downsides to consider when you are hoping to save money by switching your auto insurance provider. Perhaps the first one to plan for is the fact that you need money to save money.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

Zero money down auto insurance isn't a thing, so you'll need a cash up front to start a new policy. If you've already paid your policy in full, your current auto insurer should refund you for the unused portion of your current policy, but it doesn't happen instantly. Depending on your insurer and the processing methods they prefer, you could potentially be waiting a few weeks to get that refund check. That means, unfortunately, you'll need to have some money on hand to make the switch. Think of it like renting a new apartment — you'll need to have a deposit to get moved in.

One way to mitigate this is through monthly payment plans, which could help coordinate a changeover from one insurer to another without having to wait on a refund check. Make sure the new policy is active before you cancel the old one, otherwise you may end up flagged for a lapse in coverage. Still, if your goal is to maximize savings, you can often get a nice discount if you're willing to pay in full. What you're able to do is going to depend on your personal financial situation, so be sure to ask whether the price you're seeing is dependent on a certain payment frequency or having autopay turned on.
